Heard on I.A. No.21377/2025 , third application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C./Section 430(1) of BNSS, for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellant.

2 . Appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 366 of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 05 years and fine of Rs.5,000/-, Section 376(I) of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 11 years and fine of Rs.10,000/- and Section 376(2)(N) of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 12 years and fine of Rs.10,000/- respectively, with default stipulations.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that this Hon'ble Court has considered the question of age of victim in order dated 19.11.2024 but one crucial aspect of absence of transfer certificate for entry in scholar register of Class 6th of victim was not dealt with.

sentences.text: There are two aspects which ought to have been considered by the Trial Court and the High Court in greater detail than what has been done.
The first is the age of the prosecutrix.
The age of the prosecutrix has an extremely crucial bearing in the case.

The only evidence relied by the court for holding the prosecutrix as a minor (less than sixteen years of age), is the school register of| Government Girls High School, which was placed in the Court by the clerk of the school, Ram Sahay (PW-2).

Undoubtedly,
the date of birth in the school register is 04.04.1987 which makes the prosecutrix less'
than sixteen years of age at the time of the incident.

But it has also come in the evidence of Ram Sahay (PW-2) that this date of birth is recorded not on the statement of the parents of the prosecutrix, but by some other person and more importantly, it was based on the transfer certificate of Government Primary School where the date of birth was recorded as 3 CRA-6513-2021 04.04.1987. All the same,
this transfer certificate, on the basis of which the date of birth was recorded, was never produced in the Court.
Yet, both the Trial Court and the High Court have relied upon the veracity of the school register.
It is the same school register which marks the presence of the prosecutrix on 12.09.2000in the school.
This is also the date when the prosecutrix was allegedly raped for the first time, in the house of the appellant in village Sanwat Khera, whereas the school is at another place called Dabwali Mandi.

The Trial Court discards the evidence in the same school register, as not being authentic, when the defence had raised the apparent contradictions on the prosecutrix being in school and at the Sanwat Khera village at the same time.
This is not a fair appreciation of evidence, to say the least, as same school register is the only basis for the determination of the age of the prosecutrix!"

In the case at hand both the parents have supported the case of prosecution but both of them have deposed that they are illiterate and had got the date of birth written on a piece of paper by another person, on basis of which entry in scholar register (Exhibit P-11) was made, therefore, no transfer certificate of prosecutrix/victim was produced by the prosecution or by the parents of the victim,
hence the age of prosecutrix becomes doubtful.
She further submits that the conduct of the victim in leaving the house alone with the appellant creates suspicion.
Counsel for the appellant also submits that appellant has no previous criminal history.
This appeal is of the year 2021 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
Appellant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by the directions and conditions, which may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.

Learned counsel for the State on the other hand has opposed the application for suspension of sentence and supported the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court.
5.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6 . Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, we are of the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant can be considered.
